sections.skill: Reconcile records with the bank statement and explain differences

questions.prompt: What does reconciling mean?

choices.text: Opening a second account at another bank
Comparing your records with the bank statement
Paying all bills on the same day
Asking the bank for a loan

questions.correct_answer: Comparing your records with the bank statement
questions.intro: RECONCILING means comparing your own records with the bank statement to make sure they match. Each month, check every deposit and withdrawal. Differences usually come from: transactions the bank has not processed yet (such as a check that has not cleared), bank fees you did not record, mistakes in your records, or charges you do not recognize. Unknown charges may be errors or fraud and should be reported to the bank quickly. Reconciling catches problems while they are still small.

sections.skill: Checking a receipt against the bag

questions.prompt: In the shopping example, what is compared?
questions.correct_answer: The receipt and the bag
questions.intro: After shopping, you might compare the receipt with what is in the bag. If the receipt shows two milks but you have one, something is wrong. Reconciling is the same check for a business: your records are one list, the bank statement is the other, and you look for any item that appears on only one of them. Then you find out why.
